This savings also results in a one-time savings in energy to produce and transport the steel and cast iton and use it in the manufacture of a vehicle of the equivalent in BTU's 72,700 barrels of oil which is 0.0016 percent of the total national consumption of oil (4.5 billion barrels) in 1975. The reduction in the consumption of steel and cast iron could result in a small improvement in water quality, a small increase in industrial water supply demand and a small decrease in stationary source air pollution resulting from decreased production. However, since the reduction in the use of steel and cast iron is only 0.010 percent of total steel and cast iron production, these latter impacts should be minor.
The net savings in energy for the second viewpoint would be the equivalent of between 2.78 million barrels of oil and 9.1 million barrels of oil.
